This article documents both configuration schemas and provides all the packaged example files.

Use [Getting started](references.html) for reference retrieval and [Catalogue mapping](mapping.html) for resolution.

```{r resource-tables, include=FALSE}
# Locate the resources supplied by this package.
resources_directory <- system.file(package = "form.references")
# Read the package version used in the downloadable archive name.
resources_version <- read.dcf(file.path(resources_directory, "DESCRIPTION"), fields = "Version")[[1L]]
# Describe the files shared by the schema and example download tables.
resources_descriptions <- c(
  "references-1.0.0.yaml" = "Reference configuration schema.",
  "mapping-1.0.0.yaml" = "Catalogue mapping schema.",
  "README.md" = "Directory layout and usage notes.",
  "references.private.example.yaml" = "Public code lists and a private HTTPS registry template.",
  "references.yaml" = "Target code lists and the survey contact registry.",
  "references-source.yaml" = "Source code lists using technical identifiers.",
  "mapping.yaml" = "Station and observer correspondences between the catalogues.",
  "catalogue.csv" = "Table IDs, paths, versions, source dates and checksums.",
  "catalogue.yaml" = "Catalogue publication metadata and checksum.",
  "catalogue_aliases.csv" = "Aliases attached to individual catalogue lookups.",
  "stations.csv" = "Station reference records.",
  "observers.csv" = "Observer reference records.",
  "contacts.csv" = "Contact registry records.")
# Render website downloads, or file names for the installed package vignette.
resource_table <- function(directory, descriptions = resources_descriptions) {
  # List every file directly inside the selected resource directory.
  files <- list.files(file.path(resources_directory, directory))
  # Leave subdirectories to their own download tables.
  files <- files[!dir.exists(file.path(resources_directory, directory, files))]
  # Display the packaged file names without depending on a network connection.
  labels <- sprintf("`%s`", files)
  # Link each file to its generated website copy when building pkgdown.
  if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
    # Resolve ordinary downloads relative to this article.
    targets <- paste0("../", file.path(directory, files))
    # Absolute Markdown URLs prevent pkgdown from rewriting raw downloads to HTML pages.
    targets[endsWith(files, ".md")] <- paste0("https://ultreia-io.github.io/form.references/",
      file.path(directory, files[endsWith(files, ".md")]))
    # Render a download link for each original file.
    labels <- sprintf("[`%s`](%s)", files, targets)
  }
  # Select the descriptions for these files.
  purposes <- unname(descriptions[files])
  # Keep new files downloadable until their descriptions are added.
  purposes[is.na(purposes)] <- "Package resource."
  # Print a Markdown table for the current output format.
  cat(knitr::kable(data.frame(File = labels, Purpose = purposes), format = "pipe"), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Get the resources

```{r resource-bundle, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Offer the complete archive on the website and an offline alternative in the installed guide.
if (identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")) {
  # Link the archive containing the original schema and example directories.
  cat(sprintf("[Download all schemas and examples (%s, ZIP)](../form.references-resources-%s.zip).\n",
    resources_version, resources_version))
} else {
  # Explain where the same files are available without downloading anything.
  cat("All schemas and examples are included in the installed package.\n")
}
```

The ZIP archive preserves `schema/` and `examples/`, including both survey catalogues and their relative paths.

Its file name includes the package version; each schema retains its own format version.

Keep the survey directory together when using its configurations and correspondence CSVs locally.

You can also locate the installed resources:

```{r installed-resources, eval=FALSE}
# Locate both versioned schema files.
system.file("schema", package = "form.references")
# Locate all examples, including the private registry template.
system.file("examples", package = "form.references")
```

## Schemas

Both schemas describe package-specific YAML contracts.

Each configuration declares `schema_version: "1.0.0"`; this version identifies its format.

Catalogue publications, table revisions and correspondence data have separate versions or checksums.

```{r schema-downloads, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List every packaged schema with its download link.
resource_table("schema")
```

The schema files use these building blocks:

- `dialect`, `contract_version` and `root` identify the contract and its starting definition.
- `definitions` and `ref` define and reuse nodes.
- `type`, `properties` and `required` describe values and mandatory fields.
- `values` describes named mapping entries; `min_items` requires a minimum number of entries.
- `enum`, `min_length`, `minimum` and `exclusive_minimum` constrain individual values.
- `environment: true` permits a YAML `!env` reference at that location in a reference configuration.
- The mapping schema adds `one_of`, `sequence`, `items` and `mutually_exclusive`.

Unknown properties, duplicate keys and empty mapping keys are invalid.

YAML expressions are never evaluated. Use the package readers to validate these contracts.

## Reference configuration schema

`references-1.0.0.yaml` defines the `form.references/schema/1` dialect.

Use `reference_schema()` to inspect it and `read_reference_configuration()` to read a configuration.

Reading validates the structure and source settings without retrieving catalogue data.

### Required structure

- `schema_version` must be the string `"1.0.0"`.
- `catalogues` contains at least one named catalogue.
- Each catalogue requires `source` and `tables`; an optional `label` names it for consumers.
- `source.url` identifies an existing local directory or an HTTP(S) catalogue URL.
- `tables` contains at least one table ID, each with at least one named lookup column.
- Every lookup declares `matching: exact` or `matching: name`, plus the boolean `ignore_case`.

Table IDs and lookup names are exact declarations; lookup names identify actual columns.

Each source directory contains `catalogue.yaml`, `catalogue.csv` and the CSV files listed in that catalogue.

### Optional source settings

| Field             | Default                | Meaning                                           |
|-------------------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `cache`           | Session temporary path | Set a path explicitly to reuse files across runs. |
| `timeout`         | `60`                   | Positive request timeout in seconds.              |
| `max_connections` | `4`                    | Positive whole-number limit for CSV downloads.    |
| `user`            | Omitted                | User name for HTTPS Basic authentication.         |
| `password`        | Omitted                | Password, usually supplied through `!env`.        |

- Relative source and cache paths resolve from the configuration file's directory.
- Omitting `cache` gives each source a temporary path for the current R session.
- Supply `user` and `password` together for HTTPS Basic authentication.
- `url`, `cache`, `user` and `password` accept `!env VARIABLE`; it names an environment variable.
- With `prompt = TRUE`, the reader can securely request a missing environment password.
- A catalogue's omitted `label` defaults to its identifier when lookups are resolved.

See [private catalogue authentication](references.html#authenticate-a-private-registry-source) for the workflow.

### Survey reference configuration

This is the target configuration used by the survey examples.

```{r resources-reference-yaml, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Display the bundled reference configuration without copying it into the documentation source.
cat("```yaml\n", paste(readLines(file.path(resources_directory, "examples", "survey", "references.yaml")),
  collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

## Mapping configuration schema

`mapping-1.0.0.yaml` defines the `form.references/mapping-schema/1` dialect.

Use `mapping_schema()` to inspect it and `read_mapping_configuration()` to read a mapping.

The reader validates structure, resolves lookup defaults and checks duplicate alternative selections.

It does not retrieve catalogue data, load reference configurations or open correspondence CSVs.

### Required structure

- `schema_version` must be the string `"1.0.0"`.
- `catalogues` requires both `source` and `target`, each with `configuration` and `catalogue` names.
- `mappings` contains at least one target table ID.
- Each target declares one correspondence object or a nonempty list of alternatives.
- Every correspondence requires `source.table`.

The schema's additional building blocks describe those alternatives:

- `one_of` requires exactly one structural alternative.
- `sequence` describes an unnamed list whose entries are checked through `items`.
- `mutually_exclusive` forbids fields together; dotted paths address nested properties.

### Select the two catalogues

- `configuration` names a reference configuration supplied by the caller.
- `catalogue` selects an entry in that configuration's `catalogues` mapping.

These are names, not filesystem paths. Catalogue URLs, credentials and lookup settings stay in their configurations.

### Declare mappings by target table

Start from the required target reference, then supply the input value with its source identity.

- Each key under `mappings` is a **target catalogue table ID**.
- `source.table` identifies the source table supplying values for that target.
- Translation still runs **from source to target**.
- The same source table may appear in mappings for different target tables.

### Choose an alternative

- Use one object when a target has a single source mapping.
- Use a list when a target accepts several source mappings.
- Select one alternative using the source table, effective lookups and returned property.

**Alternatives are not fallbacks or a transformation chain.** Never select the first one or retry after a failed match.

### Lookup defaults

Each entry can override the catalogue defaults:

| Setting         | Default                       | Role                                |
|-----------------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| `source.lookup` | `catalogues.source.lookup`    | Identify the source input column.   |
| `lookup`        | `catalogues.target.lookup`    | Select the target lookup column.    |
| `property`      | The effective target `lookup` | Select the target column to return. |

Both effective lookups must be declared, either in the entry or through the catalogue defaults.

Two rules determine where the correspondence comes from:

- `source.property` and `file` are optional and mutually exclusive; there is no `mode` property.
- When the source property equals its lookup, omit `source.property` and use the input unchanged.

That shortcut performs no source lookup and does not resolve source aliases.

### Survey mapping configuration

The station entry uses a CSV; the observer entries show source-property and unchanged-input correspondences.

```{r resources-mapping-yaml, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Display the mapping used by the runnable catalogue mapping guide.
cat("```yaml\n", paste(readLines(file.path(resources_directory, "examples", "survey", "mapping.yaml")),
  collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

### Correspondence files

- `file` selects a local CSV with exactly two columns: `source_value` and `target_value`.
- Relative paths resolve from the directory containing `mapping.yaml`.
- Both columns are read as text, preserving leading zeros and literal values.
- Empty or missing values in either column are invalid correspondence data.
- File existence and CSV contents are checked during preparation, separately from YAML structure.

The survey correspondence file deliberately includes repeated, conflicting and unmatched values.

```{r resources-correspondence-csv, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Display the station correspondence file supplied with the survey example.
cat("```csv\n", paste(readLines(file.path(resources_directory, "examples", "survey", "correspondences", "stations.csv")),
  collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

See [Catalogue mapping](mapping.html) for matching order, resolution outcomes and provenance.

## Example downloads

Every file below is included in the complete archive and in the installed package.

### Survey configurations

Directory: `examples/survey/`.

```{r resources-survey, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List the survey configurations, mapping and usage notes.
resource_table("examples/survey")
```

### Mapping correspondence CSV

Directory: `examples/survey/correspondences/`.

```{r resources-correspondences, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# Describe the station file as a correspondence rather than a reference table.
resource_table("examples/survey/correspondences",
  c("stations.csv" = "Explicit source station IDs and target station codes."))
```

### Source code lists

Directory: `examples/survey/catalogue-source/code_lists/`.

These records use technical identifiers; observer names allow rebound to the target name lookup.

```{r resources-source-catalogue, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List the complete source catalogue, including metadata and lookup aliases.
resource_table("examples/survey/catalogue-source/code_lists")
```

### Target code lists

Directory: `examples/survey/catalogue/code_lists/`.

These tables contain the station and observer codes expected by the survey form model.

```{r resources-target-catalogue, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List the complete target code-list catalogue.
resource_table("examples/survey/catalogue/code_lists")
```

### Contact registry

Directory: `examples/survey/catalogue/registries/`.

```{r resources-registry, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List the contact registry used by the reference preparation examples.
resource_table("examples/survey/catalogue/registries")
```

### Private source template and overview

Directory: `examples/`.

The private-source template needs your catalogue URLs and user name before use.

```{r resources-private-template, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
# List the private HTTPS template and overview of the bundled examples.
resource_table("examples")
```

The survey form model itself is supplied by `form.model`; [Getting started](references.html) shows how to load it.

## Use the published catalogues

The same catalogue files can be retrieved directly from the website.

```{r resources-online, eval=FALSE}
# Load the catalogue retrieval functions.
library(form.references)
# Choose a temporary cache for these downloads.
resources_cache_directory <- tempfile("survey-resources-")
# Configure the published target code lists.
reference_source_configuration <- reference_source(
  "https://ultreia-io.github.io/form.references/examples/survey/catalogue/code_lists/", resources_cache_directory)
# Retrieve the station and observer tables, verifying their checksums.
reference_values <- get_reference_tables(c("observers", "stations"), reference_source_configuration)
# Configure the published contact registry.
reference_registry_source <- reference_source(
  "https://ultreia-io.github.io/form.references/examples/survey/catalogue/registries/", resources_cache_directory)
# Retrieve and verify the contact table.
reference_registry_tables <- get_reference_tables("contacts", reference_registry_source)
# Remove the temporary files created by this example.
unlink(resources_cache_directory, recursive = TRUE)
```
